gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: 5-day history of cough and runny nose. Generated HPI-001: onset about 5–6 days ago (for cough) and ROS-001: runny nose. Together they capture the same cough duration (approx. 5 days) and presence of runny nose.

Gold: cough is dry and keeps the patient up at night. Generated HPI-002: cough is dry and continuous; HPI-005: experiences nocturnal cough. These together support a dry cough that occurs at night and is consistent with sleep disturbance.

Gold: denies ear pain or sore throat. Generated ROS-002: no ear pain or discharge. Sore throat denial is not explicitly stated, but there is no contrary statement; throat irritation is attributed to coughing (HPI-004). Ear pain portion is clearly covered; sore throat portion is not directly addressed but not contradicted.

Gold: no shortness of breath or chest pain. Generated HPI-006: breathing not notably labored; HPI-007: no chest pain; HPI-008: no shortness of breath at rest; ROS-003: no significant chest pain. These collectively support absence of SOB and chest pain.
Gold: feeling tired, weak, and myalgia. Generated ROS-008: reports fatigue and general lethargy. This clearly covers tired/weak; myalgia is not explicitly mentioned but there is no contradiction.
Gold: feeling shivery, hot and cold, ?fever. Generated ROS-007: reports chills in bed; no measured fever. This supports shivery/hot-cold (chills) and the uncertain fever status (no measured fever).
Gold: no nausea/vomiting, appetite maintained. Generated ROS-004: no vomiting or nausea; ROS-006: appetite stable. Fully matches.
Gold: initial diarrhea now resolved. Generated ROS-005: diarrhea at onset but resolved. Direct match.
Gold: denies urinary symptoms or rashes. No generated fact mentions urinary symptoms or rashes; neither covered nor contradicted.
Gold: history of Type 2 diabetes and HTN. Generated PMH-001 and PMH-002 list type 2 DM and hypertension. Directly covered.
Gold: takes metformin and lisinopril. Generated MED-001 and MED-002 list metformin and lisinopril. Directly covered; later plan also references continuation.
Gold: NKDA. Generated ALLERGY-001: no known allergies. Equivalent in this context.
Gold: father has Type 2 diabetes. Generated FH-001: father with type 2 diabetes. Direct match.
Gold: lives with partner, works in IT, denies stress. Generated SH-001: lives with partner; SH-004: works as IT developer. Denial of stress is not mentioned, so that component is omitted.
Gold: ex-smoker, stopped 6 months ago. Generated SH-002: former smoker who quit about six months ago. Covered.

Gold: drinks <9 units/week. Generated SH-003: wine, 2–3 glasses on 3 nights/week. This pattern is consistent with <9 units/week depending on glass size, and does not contradict the gold fact; it refines it.
Gold: impression viral URTI. Generated ASM-001: acute viral upper respiratory infection with dry cough and rhinorrhea. Same diagnosis with extra descriptors.

Gold: supportive management with bed rest, fluids, regular paracetamol. Generated PLAN-001 (rest), PLAN-002 (fluids), PLAN-003 (paracetamol PRN). Rest and fluids match; paracetamol is PRN rather than scheduled, but both indicate paracetamol use for symptom control; no direct contradiction stated in gold regarding dosing schedule.

Gold: review in 5–7 days if not better. Generated follow-up (PLAN-004, PLAN-007, FU-002, FU-003) refer to monitor 2–3 days, reassess early next week, and follow-up if symptoms persist, but not a specific 5–7 day timeframe if no better. The explicit 5–7 day review instruction is not present.

Gold: seek review earlier for worsening symptoms such as fever, SOB, chest pain. Generated FU-001: return sooner if breathing worsens or fever develops, and PLAN-005: return if fever, worsening cough, or new chest symptoms develop. This captures earlier review for fever and respiratory/chest worsening; SOB is encompassed by breathing worsens.

Nocturnal cough is consistent with gold statement that cough keeps patient up at night.

No significant chest pain aligns with gold absence of chest pain.
No vomiting or nausea matches gold 'No nausea/vomiting.'
Diarrhea at onset but resolved matches gold initial diarrhea now resolved.
Appetite stable matches appetite maintained.
Reports chills with no measured fever is consistent with feeling shivery/hot-cold and possible fever in gold.

Gold follow-up is review in 5–7 days if not better; monitoring for 2–3 days is an additional, earlier monitoring timeframe not mentioned in gold.

Instruction to return if no improvement, cough persists, or fever/worsening cough/new chest symptoms develop is consistent with gold advice to seek earlier review for worsening symptoms such as fever, SOB, chest pain. Cough duration detail is additional but compatible.
Advice about taking time off work if contagious is not mentioned in any gold fact; it is added counseling.
Plan to reassess early next week is not specified in gold, which instead states review in 5–7 days if not better. Although somewhat similar, this specific plan/timing is new relative to gold.
Gold does not discuss antibiotic use. Statement that antibiotics are not indicated and will be considered later is additional management information.
Gold lists metformin and lisinopril but does not explicitly instruct continuation. Advising to continue current DM2 and HTN therapies is additional plan detail.
Monitoring hydration and overall status is not mentioned in gold; this is extra care guidance.
